extracted.intended_audience: early-career scientists planning to apply for the Royal Society University Research Fellowship (UK and ROI applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for applying to the Royal Society University Research Fellowship: eligibility, scope of funding, assessment process, and applicant support/adjustments. Intended to help outstanding early-career scientists prepare competitive fellowship applications and understand the review steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: URF programme objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The University Research Fellowship (URF) programme aims to support the next generation of research leaders to undertake cutting-edge research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives stated: enable outstanding early career scientists with the potential to become leaders in their field to (a) build an independent research career at a UK university or research institution, (b) gain the freedom, time, and long-term flexible support to pursue high-quality and innovative lines of scientific research, and (c) develop as research leaders via tailored professional development, networking and engagement opportunities. These programme objectives inform selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential to become a research leader
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should be outstanding early career scientists with the potential to become leaders in their field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection expects demonstration of future leadership potential through proposed research vision, independence plan, and engagement/development activities (further detail in scheme notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to build an independent research career
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fellowship should enable the applicant to build an independent research career at a UK university or research institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should explain how the award will lead to scientific independence (the interview specifically asks applicants to describe how the award will lead to independence). Host organisation support and departmental commitments are relevant evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and innovativeness of proposed research
rubrics_metrics.description: The scheme supports 'cutting-edge', 'high-quality and innovative' lines of scientific research within the Royal Society's remit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment will consider scientific validity and importance of the work (the interview aims to demonstrate importance and scientific validity). Interdisciplinary applications are handled to ensure appropriate expertise on panels and peer reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship duration and mid-fellowship review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are for eight years, with years six to eight being subject to satisfactory progress demonstrated in a mid-fellowship review at the start of year four.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation into years six–eight depends on satisfactory progress at the mid-fellowship review; applicants should be aware of and plan for this review milestone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — research experience window
rubrics_metrics.description: You have between three and eight years of research experience, excluding career breaks, since the award of your PhD by the closing date of the round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the scheme notes for further detail about the review of career breaks. Ensure you meet this window before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — employment and prior fellowship status
rubrics_metrics.description: You do not hold a permanent post (including proleptic appointment) in a university or not-for-profit research organisation and you do not hold, or have not previously held, an equivalent fellowship that provides an opportunity to establish an independent research group and therefore independent researcher status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holding a permanent post or having previously held an equivalent independence-conferring fellowship makes you ineligible; check scheme notes for nuances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — research remit (subject areas supported)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your research must be within the Royal Society’s remit of natural sciences, which includes but is not limited to biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the breakdown of subject groups and areas supported by the Royal Society for detailed scope. Applications crossing remit between Panels will be assigned a Primary Panel and seconded members as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality and visa eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can be of any nationality and those requiring a visa are eligible to apply for a Global Talent Visa under the fast-track process of endorsement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants requiring visas should check visa/endorsement eligibility and may request relocation/visa costs in the application budget (see funding uses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted uses of grant funding and maximum award
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can apply for up to a maximum of £1.87 million over eight years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds can cover contribution to the award holder’s salary; indirect and estate costs; equipment costs and research expenses including consumables, travel, etc.; contribution towards research assistance salary and associated indirect and estate costs; support for a new four-year PhD studentship(s); relocation and visa costs for the applicants and their dependants. The total grant cap may be exceeded to cover relocation/visa costs if well justified. Full funding details are in scheme notes and Royal Society Funding Guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility for personal circumstances and leave
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society provides flexibility to accommodate personal circumstances including part-time working, sabbaticals and secondments, and provision for maternity, paternity, shared parental, adoptive or extended sick leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is also provision of financial support for childcare costs that arise from attending conferences and research visits. Applicants should describe any planned or past career breaks and consult scheme notes on how these are reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment — panel assignment and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment is overseen by one of five Research Appointment Panels based on research area; applications are initially assessed by a minimum of two panel members who have the most appropriate scientific expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications crossing the remit of two Panels will be assigned to a Primary Panel and additional members will be seconded to enable appropriate interdisciplinary assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment — longlisting, independent peer review and shortlisting
rubrics_metrics.description: A longlist is drawn up; longlisted applications are subject to independent peer review; following peer review, a shortlist for interview is drawn up with oversight from the Panel Chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The multi-stage process (eligibility checks → initial panel assessment → longlist → peer review → shortlist → interview → panel recommendation) indicates that both panel expertise and external peer review influence selection; applicants should ensure written components are robust for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview — aims and assessment focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Shortlisted applicants will be invited to an in-person interview at the Royal Society. The aim of the interview is for you to demonstrate the importance and scientific validity of your work and to describe how the award will lead to your scientific independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare to articulate both the scientific case and a clear plan to achieve independence; panels will use interview performance alongside written evidence to form recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host organisation support expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Host Organisation Support – More detailed guidance provided to host organisations regarding expectations of their support for the applicant. From this round onwards, the Head of Department statement of support will be visible to applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are recommended to read this guidance in full and contact their host organisation Research Office. Evidence of departmental/host commitment is important in demonstrating feasibility of the independence plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and adjustments for disabled applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society welcomes applications from disabled scientists and provides support and adjustments to ensure full participation in the selection process; requests are made in confidentiality and are not normally shared with panel members unless relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments can include: extension of the deadline; additional support to complete the application form; receiving the application form in a different format (e.g., Word); support during interviews including technical support for accessibility software or services; additional costs that candidates may incur to attend an interview. Contact urf@royalsociety.org for confidential requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitiveness and historical success rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical data on eligible applications, offers and success rates (e.g., 2022/23: 599 eligible applications, 42 offers, 7%; 2023/24: 528 eligible applications, 34 offers, 6.4%; 2024/25: 585 eligible applications, 40 offers, 6.8%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware of the competitive nature of the scheme when preparing applications; figures are based on eligible applications and offers and do not include upgraded reserves.
